messages:
ingrid: :rotating_light: prod alert — embed route (POST /v1/embeddings) returning chat-style prose instead of numeric vectors. started ~2026-03-15T10:23:xxZ, affecting ~8% of requests for customer acme-corp. paging SRE oncall.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-2832109999 severity=P1 (automated detection: embed->gen mismatch). Notifying oncall.

pagerduty: Paging mike (sre-oncall) — escalation sent.

mike: on it. ack. Can someone paste the routing/alias mapping for embed-stable? Hypothesis: alias pinned to wrong variant.

jen: I see a recent routing pin change at 2026-03-15T10:23:11Z by eng-platform-ci. Querying model catalog now.

jen: ````
# rcli routing get alias embed-stable --json
{
  "alias": "embed-stable",
  "pinned_version": "model-chat-v1.2",
  "interface": "chat",
  "pinned_at": "2026-03-15T10:23:11Z",
  "pinned_by": "eng-platform-ci"
}
````

leo: logs show fallback path: requests routed to embedding runtime -> pinned variant incompatible -> runtime falls back to chat runtime which returns text tokens. Sample log: `route=embed-stable req_id=abcd fallback_to=chat-runtime model=model-chat-v1.2 out_type=text`.

ingrid: that pinned_version is definitely the issue — embed alias pinned to a chat variant.

mike: mitigation plan: 1) remove the pin from alias so it falls back to default embedding model 2) temporarily pin to a verified embed variant if removal is risky 3) notify CS + customers. I'll run step 1 if eng-platform approves.

jen: suggested command to remove pin (safe, config change, no deploy):
```
# remove pin
rcli routing update alias embed-stable --remove-pin --reason "critical-mis-pinned-chat-variant"
```

priya: CS: affected customers (ticket links): TKT-54321, TKT-54322. 9 orgs reported degraded embeddings -> search relevancy issues; some turned on fallback which increased latency. Marking SEV=high for these accounts.

mike: doing remove-pin now. pushing config change...

mike: ````
$ rcli routing update alias embed-stable --remove-pin --dry-run=false
Applying change...
Success: alias embed-stable unpinned (was model-chat-v1.2)
````

leo: I can confirm traffic is now hitting embed runtime and responses are numeric vectors again. Error rate dropped from 8% -> 0.3% over last 3 mins.

ingrid: :white_check_mark: mitigation validated. Notifying customer ops and closing alert.

priya: notified acme-corp and updated tickets. They saw improvement within ~2 minutes and confirmed search ingestion resumed normal behavior.

mike: creating short-lived rollback guard: pin embed-stable -> model-embed-v1.0 for extra safety while we investigate.

mike: ```
# pin to verified embed variant
rcli routing update alias embed-stable --pin model-embed-v1.0 --reason "temp-lock-after-mitigation"
```

jen: root cause likely: CI job that automated alias pins used wrong model tag (chat vs embed) — eng-platform CI used a tag mapping that got stale after last model onboarding. We'll block further automated pins until validation added.

sre-lead: Action items assigned: (1) eng-platform to add model-interface validation in pin flow (owner: jen) (2) CI removed auto-pinning for aliases until tests finish (owner: eng-infra) (3) update runbook to include quick unpin steps (owner: mike) (4) postmortem and customer follow-up (owner: priya).

mike: handing off to night oncall tasha for watch: @tasha please monitor embed error rate and any reoccurrence, I left pinned model-embed-v1.0 as guard. Full notes in INC-20260315-2832109999.

tasha: ack, taking over. will check metrics and alert if >1% error reappears.

jen: quick snippet of the bad CI diff that caused the mapping mistake (sanitized):
```
- default_alias_map["embed-stable"] = "model-embed-v1.0"
+ default_alias_map["embed-stable"] = "model-chat-v1.2"  # <- accidental
```

priya: CS to follow up with affected customers tomorrow with timeline and remediation steps.

sre-lead: Good mitigation. Please keep notes concise for postmortem. Closing notes: no data exfiltration, degraded quality only, mitigated within ~5 mins after page. Assigning postmortem meeting for 48h.

ingrid: thanks all. incident resolved for now.```
